Every Typst slides package asks you to write slides.
You open a function, you close it, and the deck's structure lives in that nesting rather than in the document.
That is comfortable to hand author and awkward to generate, so a tool that produces Typst mechanically, a Quarto filter for instance, has to build the nesting rather than emit the content.

Lanterne turns an ordinary document into a deck instead.
Headings open slides, one traversal of the body drives both the slide breaks and, later, the overlay steps, and the structure stays where the author wrote it.

::: {.callout-warning}

## Under development

The public API is not stable, and only part of it exists.
Lanterne is not published to Typst Universe, so `#import "@preview/lanterne:0.1.0": *` does not resolve; use it from a clone, as below.
Overlay steps, layouts and the element catalogue are not implemented, so `#pause` does nothing and a slide is its title and its body.
:::

## Installation

Clone the repository and import `lib.typ` by path:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mcanouil/lanterne.git
```

```typst
#import "lanterne/lib.typ": *
```

Typst 0.15.0 or newer is required.
`typst.toml` pins that floor deliberately, and the whole test suite is run against a 0.15.0 binary, so the version stated is the version verified.

## Quick start

The smallest complete deck, which is [`examples/hello-deck.typ`](https://github.com/mcanouil/lanterne/blob/main/examples/hello-deck.typ) in the repository:

```typst
#import "../lib.typ": *

#show: deck.with(
  theme: theme-tokens(
    bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"),
    fg: rgb("#1c1c22"),
    margin: 3cm,
  ),
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  slide-level: 2,
  info: (
    title: [Hello, lanterne],
    author: "Mickaël Canouil",
  ),
)

= Getting started

== What a deck is

A level 2 heading opens a slide and becomes its title.
A level 1 heading opens a section slide, which is the page before this one.
```

`deck` is the document's show rule.
It splits the body into slide records and emits one `page(...)` call per record, dressed by the theme's geometry, fonts and colours.
The deck above renders two pages: the section slide the level 1 heading opened, and the content slide the level 2 heading opened.
